cars.variant: Super Sport, James Young three-place body — 1929 Simeone reference
cars.specification_market: Early Jano 6C 1500/1750 sporting-road family; selected 1929 6C 1750 Super Sport with James Young three-place body at Simeone, chassis 312910. Museum explicitly describes road-car suitability as well as the owner's competition use. Seven attributes use this museum reference: six cylinders, quoted 1.75 L, quoted 85 hp without inferred test standard, DOHC, supercharger, coachbuilder and seating. Five family-level chassis features use Alfa Romeo's 2020 programme history and are labelled accordingly. No precise 1752-cc conversion, bore/stroke, output rpm, torque, gearbox, wheelbase, mass, speed, acceleration or originality certification imported. Group earlier 1500 relationship, 1750 SS/GS/GT labels, engine tunes, coachwork, years and chassis once. Dedicated racing/fixed-head Testa Fissa references, later 6C programmes, replicas and additional body variants are not admitted. No 102-CV fixed-head, later independent-suspension or unrelated GP-engine data transferred.
cars.summary: The early Alfa Romeo 6C sporting-road programme established Vittorio Jano's celebrated combination of a nimble chassis, twin-cam six-cylinder engineering and, in its leading sporting versions, supercharging. The 1750 family's major Mille Miglia successes and lasting place in pre-war sports-car history justify admission beyond rarity or coachwork exclusivity. Count the early 1500/1750 sporting-road family once; this James Young-bodied Super Sport reference is not a second record for each body, engine tune or racing chassis.
